headline: Daily market snapshot – July 15, 2026
summary: S&P 500 closed +0.38% at 7,543.59 and Nasdaq +0.9% at 26,107.01 on July 14 led by softer June CPI (3.5% YoY vs 3.8% expected) and strong Q2 bank earnings. VIX at 16.50; 10-yr Treasury at 4.62%; Brent crude above $85 on Hormuz tensions; gold above $4,030 on dollar weakness; DXY at 100.79.

headline: June 2026 CPI falls 0.4% monthly – largest monthly decline since April 2020 – annual rate drops to 3.5%
summary: The Consumer Price Index fell 0.4% in June on a seasonally adjusted basis, bringing the 12-month inflation rate to 3.5%, down sharply from 4.2% in May and well below the Dow Jones consensus of 3.8%. The decline was the largest single-month CPI drop since April 2020, driven by a 5.7% plunge in energy prices. Core CPI (ex-food and energy) was flat monthly, with a 2.6% annual rate.

Annual CPI 3.5% vs 3.8% consensus, down from 4.2% in May
Energy index -5.7% MoM after +3.9% in May

headline: Fed Chair Warsh testifies before Senate Banking Committee; says CPI progress not 'mission accomplished'
summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh appeared before the Senate Banking Committee on July 15 for his inaugural semiannual monetary policy testimony, following his House Financial Services debut on July 14. Warsh, who became the 17th Fed Chair on May 22, 2026, pledged vigilance on returning inflation to 2% and cautioned that the latest CPI decline does not mean 'mission accomplished,' while describing a 'sea change' in Fed thinking across five policy dimensions.
